CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  January 15, 2025-1:00 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber
  EMERGENCY SPECIAL MEETING

  Pursuant to the Declaration of Local Emergency - Windstorms and Fires issued on January 8,
  2025 the meeting was convened and held virtually by videoconference/teleconference.

  OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the emergency special meeting to order at 1:03
  p.m. (Absent: Councilmember Jones)

  ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Councilmember Rick Cole
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember Justin Jones (joined via teleconference at 1:07 p.m.)
  Councilmember Jason Lyon
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Vice Mayor Jessica Rivas

  Staff:  City Manager Miguel Marquez
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

  CONSIDERATION OF WHETHER THE CITY OF PASADENA
;  JOINS THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES TO OPT-IN TO THE
  FEDERAL EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT AGENCY (FEMA)
  DISASTER MITIGATION PROGRAM RELATED TO THE FIRE-
  DEBRIS REMOVAL AND MITIGATION

  City Manager Marquez provided introductory remarks on the item.
  Jennifer Paige, Planning Director, presented a Powerpoint
  presentation on the Federal Emergency Management Agency's
  (FEMA) disaster mitigation program in response to the Eaton fire.
  She outlined the two phases of the debris removal and mitigation
  process, noting that the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the
  California Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC), and the
  County of Los Angeles will be part of a unified command responsible
  for Phase 1 (Household Hazardous Waste Removal), and that
  Phase 2 (Private Property Debris Removal) will be managed either
  by a state or federal level agency. Director Paige stated that if the
  City participates in the program, it provides impacted property
  owners with the option to participate in these clean-up efforts,
  including structural, ash, and debris removal and soil testing. She
  noted that property owners would have 180 days to opt-in to the
  program for the cost to be covered 100% by FEMA.

  Council Minutes  1  01/15/2025
   In response to Councilmember Jones' inquiry regarding residents
  who choose not to opt-in to the program, Director Paige reported that
  residents can hire their own contractors to remove debris on their
  private property, and would be subject to the proper permitting and
  safety compliance to be administered by the City.

  Kevin McGowan, Director of LA County Office of Emergency
  Management, reported that the 180-day timeframe began when the
  disaster declaration was authorized. He reported on the two phases
  of the emergency response and clean up, cost bearings, the federal
  reassessment of reimbursement caps after the initial 180 days, and
  responded to questions.

  Discussion ensued regarding possible scenarios if the City opts out
  of Phase 2 of the debris removal and mitigation process. Director
  McGowan reported that the City could organize their own clean-up
  program, but would be subject to FEMA guidelines and would need
  to comply with all requirements in order to receive federal
  reimbursement. Additionally, private property owners could be
  responsible for their own clean-up efforts.

  In response to Councilmember Hampton's inquiry regarding the
  designated routes for debris removal, Director McGowan reported
  that the City will have input on the routes, as recovery efforts will be
  driven by local governments.

  In response to Mayor Gordo's inquiry regarding preparations for rain
  and preventing the spread of toxins, Director McGowan reported that
  the LA County Department of Public Works - Flood Control District
  will be working with cities and stakeholders to establish watershed
  assessments and develop mitigation strategies.

  Yadi, Pasadena resident, inquired about statistics on other
  disaster relief, expressed concerns regarding delayed FEMA
  reimbursements and the impacts of waiving CEQA, and
  advocated for disaster recovery and emergency response to be
  a task force or ad hoc committee project.

  MOTION:  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Hampton,
  seconded by Councilmember Masuda, to direct staff to join the
  FEMA Opt-ln Disaster Mitigation Program for fire debris removal and
  mitigation.

  AYES: Councilmembers Cole, Hampton, Jones, Lyon,
  Madison, Masuda, Vice Mayor Rivas, Mayor Gordo
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

Council Minutes  2  01/15/2025
   UPDATE - CITY RESPONSE TO WINDSTORMS AND FIRES -
  CITY MANAGER AND EMERGENCY OPERATIONS STAFF
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Consider updates from City staff and provide direction if desired
  by the City Council;
  (2) Find that, if direction is given to staff, it would not be a "project"
  subject to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant
  to California Public Resources Code Section 21065 and within the
  meaning ofCEQA Guidelines Section 15378(b).

  Chad Augustin, Fire Chief, provided an oral update on red flag
  conditions, the progressing containment of the Eaton Fire, and the
  lifting of all evacuation orders in Pasadena. He also reported that the
  incident command team is working with LA County Public Works on
  the planning for rainstorms and future mud and debris flow.

  Following brief discussion, on the order of the Mayor, and consensus
  of the City Council, the information was received and filed.
